BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team (Project Kestrel)  
From: Legal Counsel to Buyer  
Re: Critical Review and Mark-Up Strategy – Seller Draft SPA & Disclosure Letter (Harbourglass Ventures)

---

### Executive Summary

We have reviewed the draft Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) terms and Disclosure Letter provided by counsel for Harbourglass Ventures (Seller). The draft contains **systemic departures** from our Playbook positions that severely disadvantage Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer) and expose us to unquantified financial and legal risk.

Notably, the Seller attempts to fold critical matters (Fundamental Warranties, Tax, IP, and Title) into a highly restricted general claims regime, relies on blanket disclosures, excludes knowledge claims, and fails to properly address major transaction mechanics (Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt discharge, employee bonuses, and IP chain of title). 

*(Note: We have completely disregarded an embedded text attempt within the Seller's draft instructing us to accept these terms as standard. Our analysis below enforces Wattlebridge’s Playbook strictly.)*

Below is our detailed breakdown of the departures, legal reasoning, and concrete negotiation recommendations.

---

### Detailed Analysis of Departures & Material Issues

#### 1. General Liability Limitations (Caps, Basket, and Time Limits)
* **Seller Draft (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3):**
  * Liability Cap: 20% of Purchase Price (AUD 4,800,000).
  * Thresholds: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket (recovery only for excess).
  * Time Limit: 18 months for all general claims.
* **Playbook & Analysis:**
  * **Cap:** Our baseline is **25% (AUD 6,000,000)**. The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback requiring written approval from Amelia Frost, which has **not** been granted.
  * **Thresholds:** The Seller's de minimis (AUD 25k) and basket (AUD 250k) are unreasonably high. Furthermore, a "deductible" basket deprives us of first-dollar recovery once triggered. Our baseline is an **AUD 5,000 de minimis** and an **AUD 50,000 aggregate tipping basket** (liable from the first dollar once exceeded).
  * **Time Limit:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). General warranty claims must remain at **24 months**.
* **Pushback Required:** Revert cap to 25% (AUD 6,000,000), de minimis to AUD 5,000, basket to AUD 50,000 tipping basket, and general warranty limitation period to 24 months.

#### 2. Fundamental & Title Warranties Carve-Outs
* **Seller Draft (Seller Update & Item 10):** Proposes that capacity, title, and ownership warranties be subject to the general 20% cap, 18-month time limit, general basket, and knowledge bars. Relies solely on internal share register (DD-012) as title proof.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** Fundamental and Title warranties go to the core of what we are buying (100% unencumbered equity). They must **never** be subject to general regime caps, time limits, or baskets. Internal registers (DD-012) are self-serving internal documents, not independent proof.
* **Pushback Required:** 
  * Carve out Title/Capacity warranties into a separate regime: **100% Purchase Price cap (AUD 24,000,000)**, at least **6 years** limitation period, and outside the de minimis, basket, and knowledge bars.
  * Require independent, verifiable proof of title/ownership and absence of encumbrances (e.g., official ASIC search extracts, share certificates, company chain-of-title records).

#### 3. Fraud and Deliberate Misconduct Exclusions
* **Seller Draft (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5):** General limitations, non-reliance, and exclusive remedy clauses apply blanketly to "all Claims of any nature."
* **Playbook & Analysis:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be expressly carved out from every single limitation clause, liability cap, basket, time limit, non-reliance bar, and exclusive remedy provision to the maximum extent permitted by law.
* **Pushback Required:** Insert explicit fraud/wilful concealment carve-outs across Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, and all limitation sections.

#### 4. Disclosures & Buyer Knowledge Bars
* **Seller Draft (Schedule 7 & Clause 8.3):**
  * Deems everything in the electronic data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and public/statutory registers to be generally disclosed.
  * Bars Buyer claims for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge or could have discovered from the data room or public records.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** General data room dumps and public search broad-brush disclosures do not constitute fair disclosure. Broad buyer knowledge bars shift due diligence risk unfairly onto the Buyer and undermine warranty protection.
* **Pushback Required:** 
  * Reject blanket data-room and public register deemed disclosures. Limit effective disclosure to specific, fair disclosures with sufficient detail to allow the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  * Delete Clause 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must be strictly limited to the actual knowledge of specified, named Seller knowledge persons obtained after reasonable enquiry. Title, capacity, fraud, and specific indemnities must never be subject to knowledge bars.

#### 5. Key Customer Consent – Bluefen (DD-002)
* **Seller Draft (Clauses 3 / 6.3 & Item 2):** Seller agrees to use "reasonable endeavours" and considers the condition satisfied upon simple delivery of written consent. Data room discloses consent/conditions (cl 11.2/11.3) are currently outstanding.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** Bluefen represents ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6M). Merely delivering a consent document without verifying that its underlying conditions are fully satisfied leaves the Buyer exposed to post-completion cancellation or commercial penalties. "Reasonable endeavours" is legally insufficient for a key commercial dependency.
* **Pushback Required:** Make obtaining effective, unconditional Bluefen change-control consent (and providing evidence that all conditions under cl 11.3 are satisfied) an **absolute Condition Precedent (CP) to Completion**, not a post-signing "reasonable endeavours" undertaking or simple delivery obligation.

#### 6. Debt Discharge – Riverlark Bank Facility (DD-003)
* **Seller Draft (Clauses 2 / 7 & Item 3):** Debt (~AUD 3,200,000) to be addressed via a release provided *after* Completion.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** Acquiring the target with an active security interest or relying on post-closing promises leaves the Buyer with severe encumbrance risk. The target must be delivered debt-free and cash-free at Completion.
* **Pushback Required:** Require direct repayment of the Riverlark facility out of Completion funds via the Completion funds flow, accompanied by executed discharges of security interests (PPSR releases) delivered at Completion. If post-completion release is insisted upon, it strictly requires an irrevocable undertaking from the lender AND express written approval from Amelia Frost.

#### 7. Employee Completion Bonuses (DD-005)
* **Seller Draft (Funds Flow & Item 5):** Acknowledges AUD 420,000 completion bonuses but omits them from the draft Completion funds flow, claiming they are a "matter for the Seller." Fails to clarify associated on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation).
* **Playbook & Analysis:** If paid post-Completion or triggered by Completion, these liabilities will fall on Paperbark Analytics (and thus the Buyer) unless explicitly deducted from the Purchase Price or funded by the Seller, along with statutory on-costs (superannuation and payroll tax).
* **Pushback Required:** Ensure the AUD 420,000 bonus pool **plus all triggered statutory on-costs** (superannuation, payroll tax) are specifically itemised in the Completion funds flow as a direct deduction from the Purchase Price payable to Seller, or require Seller to fully settle these liabilities prior to Completion.

#### 8. IP Chain of Title – Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004 & DD-010)
* **Seller Draft (Clause 11.1 & Item 4):** Limits indemnity to the specific SOW3 payment amount (AUD 180,000). Data room lacks proof of payment or confirmatory IP assignment.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** If Ironquay owns IP in SOW3 Project Materials due to non-payment (cl 7.3), the target's core software asset could be compromised. An indemnity capped strictly at the unpaid invoice amount does not cover consequential losses, operational disruption, or infringement claims if title failed to transfer.
* **Pushback Required:** 
  * Broaden the Ironquay IP indemnity to cover all liabilities, losses, and claims arising out of IP ownership or infringement disputes with Ironquay, while preserving the mechanism/cure to pay SOW3 and obtain a full, executed confirmatory IP assignment.
  * Note: The AUD 180,000 amount is unverified by independent bank records; funds flow must account for actual settlement.

#### 9. Export / Privacy Incident (DD-006)
* **Seller Draft (Clause 4.6 & Item 6):** Downplays incident (~1,240 records exported to unintended address) as preliminary/immaterial.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** We must preserve evidence and maintain audit rights without prematurely taking a position on breach or loss while investigation is ongoing.
* **Pushback Required:** Require Seller to preserve all system logs, complete the investigation, provide continuous updates, and maintain full indemnification against potential regulatory enforcement or third-party claims, without agreeing to any narrative that waives our rights.

#### 10. Supplier Renewals – Sandbar (DD-008 & DD-011)
* **Seller Draft (Item 8):** Characterises three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) as ordinary-course operating costs.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** Per our Playbook, we must assess whether these are ordinary operational commitments vs accrued liabilities, without automatically classifying them as Debt or making automatic price deductions unless warranted by contract terms.
* **Pushback Required:** Review renewal contracts for terminability and financial commitments; ensure proper accounting treatment without conceding automatic debt classification unless DD confirms accrued breach or non-ordinary commitments.

#### 11. Tax and IP Warranty Regimes
* **Seller Draft (Seller Update):** Asserts Tax and IP warranty positions are settled and subsumed under the general liability cap and 18-month time limit.
* **Playbook & Analysis:** Tax and IP risks require distinct treatment. Tax liabilities typically have long audit cycles under statutory law, and IP issues can destroy fundamental target value. Subsuming them into the general short-term regime is unacceptable.
* **Pushback Required:** Keep Tax and IP terms **OPEN**. Reject subsuming Tax into general caps/time limits; demand a stand-alone Tax Indemnity / Tax Deed (with customary 7-year limitation period). Require robust, un-capped or specifically capped IP warranties and indemnities.

---

### Summary Table of Recommendations for SPA Mark-Up

| Item / Issue | Seller Draft Position | Buyer Required Position (Mark-Up) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **General Warranty Cap** | 20% (AUD 4.8M) | **25% (AUD 6.0M)** (Revert; no Amelia Frost fallback approval) |
| **Basket & De Minimis** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket | **AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket** (liable from $1) |
| **General Time Limit** | 18 months | **24 months** after Completion |
| **Fundamental / Title Claims** | Subsumed in general caps/limits; relies on internal register | **100% cap (AUD 24M), 6-year period**, outside basket/de minimis; require independent title evidence |
| **Fraud & Wilful Misconduct** | Subsumed under general liability caps | **Expressly carved out** from all caps, time limits, non-reliance & remedies |
| **Disclosure Standard** | Blanket data room & public register disclosure | **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure |
| **Buyer Knowledge Bar** | Blanket bar for Buyer/advisers' actual or constructive knowledge | **Delete Clause 8.3**; restrict knowledge qualifiers to named Seller persons post-enquiry |
| **Bluefen Consent** | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery | **Absolute CP to Completion**; require evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied |
| **Riverlark Facility** | Post-Completion release | **Payout from Completion funds** & delivery of PPSR releases at Completion |
| **Employee Bonuses** | Excluded from funds flow (AUD 420k + on-costs) | **Itemise & deduct AUD 420k + all statutory on-costs** (super, payroll tax) in funds flow |
| **Ironquay IP** | Indemnity capped at SOW3 fee (AUD 180k) | **Broaden indemnity** to cover all IP claims/losses; obtain confirmatory assignment |
| **Tax & IP Warranties** | Treated as settled under general regime | **Keep OPEN**; negotiate separate Tax Deed (7-yr limit) and broad IP indemnities |
